comments: Candidate fixes all leaks (payments filtered by ts, reviews by creation date, mutable order_status replaced by dated delivery/carrier events before seed_time), keeps the same product-level aggregation families, and dropping canceled_share is required for temporal safety since status is mutable post-seed.

Candidate fixes the review leakage by filtering on review_answer_timestamp < seed_time and adds properly time-gated payment/delivery features while retaining the original sales/review feature families, though a NameError (fill_zero vs fill_zero list defined as 'fill_zero' but referenced correctly—actually defined as fill_zero) and minor naming slips (n_sellers vs n_sellers fill) risk runtime failure without introducing new temporal leakage.

Candidate fixes review fallback (empty instead of unfiltered) and gates deliveries/payments on timestamps, but payment filtering is conditional on a 'ts' column whose existence is unknown, so residual payment leakage cannot be ruled out from code alone.

Candidate keeps all original feature families (order/item/price/recency/review/payment aggregates) while tightening time filtering (strict ts < seed_time, review_creation_date <= seed_time, no delivery/answer timestamps) and only adds derived features like trends and revenue windows.

Candidate fixes the unfiltered payments (and payment_type vocabulary) by filtering on ts <= seed_time and keeps reviews filtered by review_creation_date, while retaining all original feature families with only additive changes (180-day window, avg_payment_value); reliance on items['ts'] as the purchase timestamp is assumed but not verifiable from code alone.

Candidate masks delivery/approval/estimate diffs and is_delivered by seed_time (replacing mutable order_status), filters seller_agg via time-filtered order_items, and retains all original feature families.

Candidate masks delivery/approval/carrier timestamps and order status by seed_time, filters order_items and seller aggregation by ts (fixing the unfiltered seller_agg leak), and retains all original feature families with only minor aggregate trims.

Candidate correctly masks future delivery/approval dates and filters the previously unfiltered order_items for seller_agg, but still uses the mutable current order_status (delivered_ratio) without any as-of-seed_time check, so status-based leakage remains.

The candidate fixes the review leakage by filtering reviews to review_creation_date <= seed_time and keeps all original feature families (windowed sales, recency, reviews) while adding only seed_time-observable features like order status shares.
Candidate correctly gates reviews by review_creation_date, payments by ts, and delivery features by delivered_customer_date <= seed_time while retaining all original feature families and aggregates.

Candidate filters reviews by review_creation_date, delivery/carrier/estimated dates by seed_time availability, and payments by ts <= seed_time while retaining all original feature families (aggregates, windows, payment-type shares) plus additions; minor residual reliance on a 'ts' column existing in payments is unverifiable from code alone.

Reviews, payments, and delivery dates are now gated by timestamps before seed_time, but delivered_rate still uses the mutable order_status field without verifying the delivery occurred before seed_time, and reliance on possibly absent 'ts' columns in reviews/payments leaves runtime correctness unclear.

Candidate fixes the unfiltered review merge (and order/payment joins) with explicit timestamp cutoffs before seed_time, keeps all original feature families, and only adds new time-safe features like delivery status and payment aggregates.

Candidate fixes the leaks by filtering payments on ts, reviews on review_creation_date, and masking delivery dates at/after seed_time, while retaining all original feature families and only adding new ones.

Candidate filters orders by purchase timestamp, reviews by review_creation_date, and payments by ts, and masks delivery-derived features to deliveries on/before seed_time, while retaining all original feature families plus allowed additions; residual uncertainty comes from reliance on a 'ts' column in payments/order_items whose semantics are not shown.

Candidate gates reviews by review_creation_date, payments by ts, and delivery/on-time/delivered features by delivered_customer_date <= seed_time, removing future leakage while retaining all original feature families and aggregation logic.

Reviews and delivery delay are now seed_time-filtered, but leakage remains: order_status (mutable, may be set after seed_time) still drives is_canceled/delivery flags, and payments are aggregated without filtering on the computed pay_ts, so post-seed payments/status can inform features.

Candidate filters reviews by review_creation_date, deliveries by delivered date, and items by ts before seed_time, removing the delayed-review/delivery leakage while keeping all original feature families and adding only new ones.

Original joined reviews without any date filter (delayed-review leakage); candidate filters reviews by review_creation_date <= seed_time and gates delivery features on order_delivered_customer_date <= seed_time, while keeping all original feature families and adding only consistent new ones.

Candidate now gates reviews on review_creation_date < seed_time, payments/items on ts < seed_time, and delivery/delay features on actual pre-seed_time delivery dates (unused order_status is harmless), while retaining all original sales, recency, review, and was_sold families plus permitted additions.
